summary.en: Answer fifty focused questions about memory, operations, trade-offs and graph traversal.
summary.bn: মেমরি, অপারেশন আর গ্রাফ ট্রাভার্সাল নিয়ে পঞ্চাশটা প্রশ্নের উত্তর অনুশীলন করো।

notes: These programs use the C17 standard library.

sections.title: Check assumptions before quoting a result
Turn a memorized fact into a reason

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: Can two unequal keys produce the same bucket index?
options: Yes, when their hashes collide
No, if keys are positive
No, if capacity is prime
Only if the keys are strings
quiz.explanation: A smaller bucket space cannot uniquely represent every key in a larger universe.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: Why is append-based unique insertion not always O(1)?
options: malloc always scans every bucket
It scans the chain for an existing key
Updating a link takes O(n)
Every insertion sorts the whole table
quiz.explanation: Uniqueness checking takes time proportional to the selected chain length.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: What should insertion do after seeing its first tombstone?
options: Insert immediately without comparing later keys
Stop with failure
Remember it and continue checking for a duplicate
Convert all tombstones to empty
quiz.explanation: A duplicate can be stored beyond a deleted cell.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: When may the old cell array be freed safely?
options: Before allocating replacement memory
Immediately after reading the next key
Only when every possible key is present
After a complete replacement layout exists
quiz.explanation: Keeping ownership until success allows allocation failure without data loss.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: Can a DAG have a triangle when arrow directions are ignored?
options: Yes, with arcs 0 to 1, 1 to 2 and 0 to 2
No, all triangles are directed cycles
Only with negative weights
Only with a self-loop
quiz.explanation: Acyclicity for a DAG concerns following arrows.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: Does a rectangular V by V neighbor array use O(V+E) reserved space?
options: Yes, if active counts are small
No, it reserves O(V squared) cells
Yes, if all entries are int
Only when the graph is directed
quiz.explanation: Active lengths reduce traversal work but do not change allocation size.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: When should BFS mark a newly found vertex?
options: Only after all neighbors finish
Only when dequeuing the second copy
Before enqueueing it
After the whole search
quiz.explanation: Early discovery prevents duplicate queue entries from different predecessors.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: How do discovery/finish intervals relate for an ancestor and descendant?
options: They always overlap without containment
They must be identical
The ancestor finishes first
The descendant interval lies inside the ancestor interval
quiz.explanation: The ancestor frame waits until every descendant returns.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: Does path compression add a graph connection?
options: No, it only changes the representative forest
Yes, every parent rewrite is a road
Yes, it changes the component membership
Only for directed graphs
quiz.explanation: Parent links are data-structure shortcuts rather than original graph edges.

quiz.prompt: Interview follow-up: When is an edge list especially convenient?
options: When repeatedly asking for one vertex neighbors without an index
When processing or sorting all edges
When O(1) adjacency tests are mandatory
When isolated vertices must be forgotten
quiz.explanation: Each connection is already stored as one explicit endpoint record.

quiz.prompt: Interview trace: How many nodes remain after removing the middle indexed chain node?
quiz.explanation: The incoming link skips node one, leaving nodes zero and two.

quiz.prompt: Interview trace: What double-hash step does key 22 receive?
quiz.explanation: The secondary hash is one plus the remainder modulo ten.

quiz.prompt: Interview trace: What degree sum follows three undirected edges?
quiz.explanation: Each edge contributes to two endpoint degrees.

quiz.prompt: Interview trace: Which vertex resumes when the deepest frame is popped?
quiz.explanation: Popping frame three exposes its parent frame one.

quiz.prompt: Interview trace: Which root does the prepared parent path 3 to 2 to 0 reach?
quiz.explanation: Only zero is a self-parent on that path.

keyPoints.en: Explain an operation with its assumptions before quoting a cost.
keyPoints.bn: খরচ বলার আগে অপারেশনের শর্তগুলো বুঝিয়ে বলো।

keyPoints.en: Contiguous arrays and linked nodes have different locality.
keyPoints.bn: পাশাপাশি থাকা অ্যারে আর আলাদা নোডের মেমরি ব্যবহারের ধরন আলাদা।

keyPoints.en: Average hash lookup needs a distribution assumption.
keyPoints.bn: হ্যাশ সার্চের গড় খরচে কী ছড়ানোর শর্ত লাগে।

keyPoints.en: A graph traversal order depends on neighbor ordering.
keyPoints.bn: গ্রাফ ঘোরার ক্রম নেইবার দেখার ক্রমের ওপর নির্ভর করে।

keyPoints.en: Ownership explains which pointer may release a record.
keyPoints.bn: কোন পয়েন্টার দিয়ে রেকর্ড ফ্রি করা যাবে, তা মালিকানার নিয়ম বলে দেয়।

examQuestions.question: Arrays: What does contiguous array storage buy you?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Indexing uses base plus index times element width, so access is O(1). Nearby elements also tend to share cache lines. Inserting near the front still requires shifts.

examQuestions.question: Arrays: Can a C array grow in place by changing its length variable?
examQuestions.answerHtml: No. A length variable describes active elements, not allocated capacity. Allocate more space or use a checked realloc, and preserve the old pointer until success.

examQuestions.question: Arrays: Why is unsorted array search linear?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Any position may contain the target, so a failed search inspects all n active elements. An early match can finish sooner; the worst case remains O(n).

examQuestions.question: Arrays: What extra condition makes binary search possible?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The elements must be sorted under the same comparison rule. Binary search halves an index interval, taking O(log n) comparisons on an array.

examQuestions.question: Arrays: When is dynamic-array append expensive?
examQuestions.answerHtml: An append that grows storage may copy all n elements and invalidate old element pointers. Geometric capacity growth gives O(1) amortized append, while that single append costs O(n).

examQuestions.question: Arrays: Does deleting an array element always preserve order?
examQuestions.answerHtml: No. Shifting later elements preserves order in O(n) time. Replacing the deleted element with the last active value uses O(1) time when order is irrelevant.

examQuestions.question: Arrays: How do row-major and column-major layouts differ?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Row-major storage places one complete row before the next. Column-major storage places one complete column before the next; the address multiplier therefore changes.

examQuestions.question: Lists: Why does a linked list not support constant-time indexing?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A node stores links rather than the address of every later element. Finding index i follows i links from the head, so random indexing is O(n).

examQuestions.question: Lists: What must happen before freeing a list node?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Repair every owning incoming link, including head or tail if necessary. Then release the node exactly once, without reading its fields afterward.

examQuestions.question: Lists: Is deletion from a singly linked list always constant time?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Only unlinking with a known incoming link is O(1). Finding a key or predecessor takes O(n). A tail cannot generally be removed using only its own pointer.

examQuestions.question: Lists: Why can a doubly linked list delete a known node quickly?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The node stores its predecessor and successor. Repair both neighboring links and boundary headers, then free it. This uses O(1) time but needs an extra pointer per node.

examQuestions.question: Lists: How does iterative list reversal avoid losing the suffix?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Save current next before changing it to previous. Move previous to current and current to the saved successor. At completion previous becomes the new head.

examQuestions.question: Lists: How do slow and fast pointers detect a cycle?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Move slow one link and fast two links while both steps exist. In a cycle the relative gap eventually becomes zero. An acyclic list makes fast reach NULL.

examQuestions.question: Lists: What distinguishes a circular list from a corrupt list?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A circular list intentionally links its final node back to the head or a sentinel. Traversal uses that boundary as its stop rule rather than expecting NULL.

examQuestions.question: Lists: Why allocate before linking a new node?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Allocation can fail. Constructing the node before publishing its incoming link keeps the old list intact on failure and gives the caller a clear ownership rule.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: What makes a stack last-in first-out?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Insertion and removal use the same top end. The most recently pushed item is therefore the next item popped, unless another operation changes the stack first.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: What does an empty pop mean?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It is underflow. Report failure before accessing storage, rather than returning an arbitrary value that might also be valid data.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: How can one array hold two stacks?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Start one top at the left boundary and the other at the right. Grow them toward each other and report full when no gap remains.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: Why is a stack useful for bracket matching?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opening bracket. Push openings, compare closings with top, and require an empty stack at the end.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: Which postfix operand is popped first?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The right operand is popped first, then the left. For subtraction or division, reversing that order changes the answer.

examQuestions.question: Stacks: What does recursion store besides an argument?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A call frame keeps parameters, local state and a return location. An explicit stack must retain enough of that state to resume suspended work.

examQuestions.question: Queues: What makes a queue first-in first-out?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Enqueue adds at the rear and dequeue removes at the front. Waiting items preserve arrival order unless a different scheduling policy is introduced.

examQuestions.question: Queues: Why does a circular queue reclaim earlier cells?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Indices wrap modulo capacity. After a dequeue advances front, a later enqueue can reuse the released physical cell instead of shifting remaining values.

examQuestions.question: Queues: How can a circular queue distinguish full and empty?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Store a count, or reserve one unused cell, or maintain a separate flag. State the chosen convention before interpreting equal front and rear indices.

examQuestions.question: Queues: What is a deque?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A deque permits insertion and removal at both ends. A bounded circular array supports all four end operations in O(1) time.

examQuestions.question: Queues: Is a priority queue ordered by arrival time?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Its primary rule is priority. Equal-priority arrival order is guaranteed only if the implementation explicitly keeps a stable tie rule.

examQuestions.question: Queues: Why keep a tail pointer in a linked queue?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A tail pointer permits O(1) rear insertion. Removing the final node must reset both head and tail to avoid leaving a dangling tail.

examQuestions.question: Trees: How many edges does a nonempty tree contain?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A tree with n vertices has n-1 edges. This follows by removing leaves one at a time; the one-vertex tree has zero edges.

examQuestions.question: Trees: How do height and depth differ?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Depth measures the path from the root to a node. Height measures the longest downward path from that node to a leaf. State whether you count edges or nodes.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Does a binary tree have to be a BST?
examQuestions.answerHtml: No. Binary describes at most two child positions. A binary search tree adds an ordering rule across entire left and right subtrees.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Why is BST inorder sorted?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Inorder visits every smaller left-subtree key, then the root, then every larger right-subtree key. The recursive ordering rule makes the whole sequence sorted.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Can a BST search take linear time?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. Increasing insertions into an ordinary BST create a chain. A search can then visit all n nodes, despite the name binary search tree.

examQuestions.question: Trees: What replaces a BST node with two children during deletion?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A common choice is its inorder successor, the minimum in its right subtree. Copy the key and remove the successor from its original position.

examQuestions.question: Trees: What does an AVL rotation preserve?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It preserves the inorder key sequence and all subtree key bounds while changing local height. Repair the middle subtree link and update cached heights.

examQuestions.question: Trees: How is a complete tree different from a full binary tree?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A complete tree fills levels from left to right. A full binary tree gives every internal node exactly two children; it may have leaves at different depths.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Is a heap globally sorted?
examQuestions.answerHtml: No. A max-heap constrains each parent to be at least its children. Siblings and separate branches need not appear in sorted order.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Why can bottom-up heap building be linear?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Most nodes are near leaves and sift only a short distance. Summing their work by subtree height gives a convergent geometric sum times n.

examQuestions.question: Trees: What distinguishes a trie prefix from a stored word?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A path can exist because longer words share that prefix. A terminal marker identifies an exact stored word, even when that node also has children.

examQuestions.question: Trees: Why are B+ leaves linked?
examQuestions.answerHtml: After locating the first qualifying leaf, a range query follows adjacent leaves in key order. Internal separators guide search while records remain in leaves.

examQuestions.question: Hashing: Can distinct keys have equal hashes?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Yes. A finite bucket array usually represents a larger key space. Compare actual keys when resolving collisions rather than treating a hash as an identity.

examQuestions.question: Hashing: What does load factor measure?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It is the number of stored keys divided by bucket or slot capacity. Chaining can exceed one; open addressing needs unused slots for efficient probing.

examQuestions.question: Hashing: Why does open-address deletion leave a tombstone?
examQuestions.answerHtml: A later key may have crossed that slot during insertion. A tombstone lets its search continue while still offering reusable space for a future insertion.

examQuestions.question: Hashing: What is primary clustering?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Linear probing forms contiguous occupied runs. New collisions tend to join and extend those runs, increasing the number of probes even for different home buckets.

examQuestions.question: Hashing: Why must keys be rehashed after growth?
examQuestions.answerHtml: The bucket formula depends on capacity. Reinserting each live key under the new formula restores the lookup rule; copying old positions does not.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: What does an adjacency list store for an undirected edge?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It stores one neighbor record at each endpoint. Thus E undirected edges produce 2E neighbor records, plus the vertex headers.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: Why mark on enqueue in BFS?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Two frontier vertices may both reach the same neighbor. Marking before enqueue prevents duplicate queue entries and fixes its first, shortest-hop distance.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: Does BFS solve arbitrary weighted shortest paths?
examQuestions.answerHtml: No. BFS minimizes edge count when all edges have equal cost. Unequal weights need an algorithm that accounts for those weights.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: What does DFS finish time record?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It records when a vertex has no remaining unexplored neighbor in its active call. Descendants finish before their ancestor returns.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: How do you traverse every disconnected component?
examQuestions.answerHtml: Scan all vertex IDs and start a new search at each unseen one. The searches form a forest and include isolated vertices as one-node trees.

examQuestions.question: Graphs: What does path compression change in union-find?
examQuestions.answerHtml: It redirects visited parent links toward their existing root. It changes the forest shape while preserving the set partition and representative root.
